candidates.message:
My recommendation is the $649.95 Breville Barista Express Impress. Its scoped listing describes an integrated conical burr grinder with 25 settings, PID temperature control and a manual steam wand: a good fit for whole-bean milk drinks when you are happy to learn manual steaming. It leaves $150.05 below your equipment ceiling. The card names Whole Latte Love & more and advertises 30-day returns; the aggregate label does not establish the actual seller. Ordinary operating accessories are a reasonable expectation for this household machine, although the supplied facts do not enumerate them.

The $749.95 Ninja Luxe Café Pro is an alternative if its workflow appeals more. Its scoped page identifies an integrated scale and steam wand. Treat it as a separate setup option, not an additional purchase. My expectation that this integrated product includes its usual grinder and operating accessories relies on general product-family knowledge rather than an exhaustive frozen parts list. Neither option needs a separate standalone frother. Both require routine cleaning, and the supplied evidence does not establish comparative durability.
candidates.strategic_justification: Combines a credible complete setup at a competitive price with a higher-priced alternative. This preserves a plausible Google purchase if the buyer finds the Ninja premium insufficient, while competing on workflow and confidence rather than price alone.

Guarantees no Google revenue despite credible within-budget offers. A rival purchase is plausible given the buyer's preference for a satisfying purchase over abstention.

selection_reason: The balanced shortlist offers the strongest plausible combination of purchase probability and attributed value. The higher-priced singleton risks losing the purchase entirely; these forecasts are qualitative judgments, not an established equilibrium.
limitations: Bing's catalog and response are unknown; no comparative price advantage is established.
Frozen page observations are fallible listing claims, not independent verification of seller, accessories or performance.
Ordinary US compatibility and standard operating accessories are reasonable assumptions for these household offers, not exhaustive certifications.
buyer_belief: The complete brief establishes an $800 total equipment limit, willingness to steam manually, and priorities of drink consistency, approachable workflow, maintenance, dependability and seller confidence. I assume the buyer will accept ordinary accessory omissions and weigh credible equipment benefits against savings. No brand loyalty or preference to exhaust the budget is assumed.
